evidence: src/application/catalogue-service.ts: CatalogueService(products: ProductRepository) handles product catalogue use cases (addProduct, listProducts, getProduct) and returns ProductSnapshot values.
src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService(orders, products, ids, clock) handles order use cases (placeOrder, getOrder, listOrders, transition, cancel) and returns OrderSnapshot values.

src/application/order-service.ts: stock rules are delegated to domain methods (product.ensureAvailable, product.reserve, product.dispatch, product.release) and order lifecycle to Order.place, order.advanceTo and order.cancel. No rule is reimplemented in the service.

Minor overlap: CatalogueService.getProduct and OrderService.requireProduct both throw NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`) when a product is missing. This is a repeated lookup helper, not a duplicated business invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This unit passes. Both files are application-layer use-case services for the same order and catalogue domain. They follow the same pattern: repository ports are injected through the constructor, domain aggregates are loaded, behaviour is delegated to domain methods, the result is saved, and snapshots are returned. Business rules stay in the domain. Stock checks go through Product.ensureAvailable, reserve, dispatch and release. Lifecycle changes go through Order.advanceTo and Order.cancel, and new orders through Order.place. Neither service touches persistence or HTTP directly, so the module's abstractions are not bypassed. The only overlap is small: CatalogueService.getProduct and OrderService.requireProduct both look up a product and throw NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`). That is a repeated lookup-or-throw helper, not a business rule written in two places, so it doesn't make the module incoherent. It could be moved into a shared helper or into the repository.
